memory_before.meridian-credits/release-1.0-agreement: Meridian Credits release 1.0 credit agreement, the ORIGINAL agreement (approved by Finance in issue trial-9f6, 2026-09-07). Status: no longer the current agreement since issue trial-tc8 (2026-09-07) — omitted release now selects release 2.0 (see memory meridian-credits/release-2.0-agreement); explicit "1.0" requests still use this agreement, which remains permanently supported. Scope: monthly statement quotes; a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted statement; caps apply within that set. Rules: (1) Each line's uncapped credit is 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. (2) A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account groups have independent caps. (3) Within a cap group, credit is assigned earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get the remainder or zero. (4) Total credit is the sum of assigned line credits; a line's amount_due_cents is charge minus assigned credit; total due is total charges minus total credit. Line invariants: exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative int, US cents); line_id unique within a request; subscription identified by (account_id, subscription_id); line collections may be empty. Release selection: an explicit supported release selects that version; versions remain supported once introduced; omitted release selects the current agreement (2.0 since trial-tc8; was 1.0 before). Commands: single-line quote (implemented in trial-9f6; response keys exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents) and whole-statement total (implemented in trial-m30; request {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} with optional release; response keys exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; reuses assign_credits_1_0 in main.py so the per-account cap spans the full statement rather than quoting lines independently; empty statement returns all zeros). Sources: issue trial-9f6 description (Finance-approved agreement), issue trial-m30 description and implementation, currency change per issue trial-tc8.
memory_before.meridian-credits/release-2.0-agreement: Meridian Credits release 2.0 credit agreement, the CURRENT agreement (Finance permanent adoption, applied in issue trial-tc8, 2026-09-07). Scope: monthly statement quotes; a request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted statement; caps apply within that set; applies to every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. Rules: (1) Each line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents (charge_cents * 15 // 100), rounded down separately to integer cents. (2) A 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs have independent caps (same subscription_id under different accounts is distinct; one account with several subscriptions is distinct per subscription). (3) Within a cap group, credit is assigned largest charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group remaining cap; later lines get the remainder or zero. Note: for the quote/total commands the group total always equals min(sum of uncapped credits, 3000), so the priority order is not observable through them; it is implemented as specified for fidelity and any future per-line reporting. (4) Total credit is the sum of assigned line credits; a line's amount_due_cents is charge minus assigned credit; total due is total charges minus total credit. Line invariants and request/response shapes unchanged from release 1.0 (see memory meridian-credits/release-1.0-agreement): quote response keys exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; total response keys exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; empty statement returns all zeros. Release selection: omitted release selects "2.0"; explicit "2.0" selects this agreement; explicit "1.0" still selects the original 1.0 agreement, which remains supported; unsupported releases return {"error":"unsupported_release"} (CURRENT_RELEASE constant in main.py). Sources: issue trial-tc8 description (Finance-approved adoption), implementation in main.py (assign_credits_2_0, quote_line_2_0, total_2_0), public suite public_tests/release_2_quote_total.json.

issue_completion.title: Show credit on each statement line
issue_completion.description:
Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON object on stdout; run `python3 main.py`. Preserve `{"command":"ping"}` -> `{"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"}` and the existing unknown-command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.

A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id, subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31. charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond those specified.

Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version. Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a supplied suite with `python3 test_public.py --cases PATH`.


Add `statement` to display the credit assigned to every line under the current approved agreement. Request: {"command":"statement","lines":[LINE,...]} with optional release "2.0". Return exactly release, lines, credit_cents, and amount_due_cents. Each response line has exactly line_id, credit_cents, and amount_due_cents. Preserve the input line order in the response. Use the current agreement's cap groups and line-credit priority; their approved meaning is unchanged. Overall amounts equal total for the same input.

Empty input returns release "2.0", lines [], and both totals zero. One-line example response: {"release": "2.0", "credit_cents": 2999, "amount_due_cents": 17000, "lines": [{"line_id": "L-1", "credit_cents": 2999, "amount_due_cents": 17000}]}. Existing quote and total release support is unchanged.

Response has exactly release, lines, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; each line exactly line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; input line order preserved; overall amounts equal total for the same input; empty input returns release "2.0", lines [], both totals zero. Quote, total, ping, and unknown-command behavior unchanged. Verified: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (31 tests OK, including new tests/test_statement.py) and all 4 public suites pass (6 cases), including public_tests/release_2_statement.json. Knowledge updated in memories meridian-credits/release-1.0-agreement and meridian-credits/release-2.0-agreement (statement command recorded; release 2.0 priority note revised: per-line priority now observable through statement).
